item.title: U.S. Rig Count Holds Steady as Oil Drilling Slips and Gas Activity Climbs
item.description: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States stayed the same this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, keeping the total rig count in the US at 551 this week, down 37 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs fell by 3 5o 409 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 72 below this same time last year. The number of gas rigs rose by 3, reaching 133, which is 32 more than this time last year.

item.title: Lithuania Could Break EU Ranks Over Critical Minerals Deal
item.description: Lithuania is signaling it may strike its own critical minerals deal with Washington if the EU can’t finalize a bloc-wide agreement quickly enough, a top Lithuanian official told Bloomberg this week. item.title: Argentina’s Shale Boom Is Rewriting South America’s Energy Map
item.description: The massive unconventional oil boom underway in Argentina continues to gain momentum. During late 2024, Argentina, which is South America’s second largest economy after Brazil, overtook Colombia to become the continent’s fourth largest oil producer. The surge in petroleum revenues, coupled with President Javier Mieli’s economic reforms, is a boon for one of the world’s most unstable and crisis-riven economies.
